data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense relies on 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) to justify preferring better-corroborated theories without induction, but this fails because Popper's own formal definition of verisimilitude was proven logically incoherent by Tichý and Miller (1974). They demonstrated that under Popper's criteria, a false theory with more content cannot be ranked as closer to the truth than another false theory unless it entails the truth-content of the other, which is unknowable. Consequently, the 'pragmatic rule' the target proposes lacks the logical foundation it claims to have within Popper's system; without a coherent metric for verisimilitude, the preference for the 'better-corroborated' theory collapses back into an unjustified inductive assumption that past survival predicts future success or proximity to truth, exactly the smuggling of induction the prompt asks to identify.
